snippet.title: Metropolis: Alexandria
snippet.description:
Step back in time to explore Alexandria—the ancient world’s greatest city of knowledge, culture, and innovation. Discover its secrets buried beneath modern streets!

Uncover how Alexandria became the Mediterranean’s crown jewel, from its founding by Alexander the Great to its rise as a vibrant melting pot of cultures, commerce, and scientific achievement. This video dives into the stories behind legendary landmarks like the Lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and the legendary Library of Alexandria, home to the era’s greatest scholars and over 700,000 scrolls of learning. Journey with archaeologists as they reveal Alexandria’s massive city planning, advanced water systems, and remnants of daily life that shaped thousands of years of history.

Meet fascinating historical figures such as Agnodike, a pioneering woman who defied the odds to pursue medicine in a society where knowledge was power but forbidden to women. Investigate bold discoveries—from the sprawling catacombs under Com el Shokafa to papyrus scrolls preserved in the desert—shedding light on everyday life, ancient production techniques, and multicultural harmony that defined the city’s golden age. See how Alexandria thrived under the Ptolemies before encountering Roman conquest and learn what still lies hidden beneath the city today.

Whether you’re intrigued by ancient engineering, lost knowledge, or the extraordinary diversity of this Mediterranean metropolis, join us as we unlock the spectacular legacy of Alexandria—the true city ahead of its time.

#History #Alexandria #AncientEgypt #LibraryOfAlexandria #LighthouseOfAlexandria #Archaeology #AlexanderTheGreat #PtolemaicDynasty #AncientCities #WorldWonders

snippet.title: Is This The Most Dangerous Country To Report The Truth?
snippet.description:
Through conversations with reporters, editors, cartoonists, and Kurdish war correspondents, the documentary reveals a country where journalism has become dangerous work. Newsrooms face political pressure, self-censorship, police raids, lawsuits, and public intimidation — yet many journalists continue speaking out despite the risks.

The film explores:

- The collapse of press freedom in Turkey
- Fear, censorship, and political polarization in the media
- Journalists losing jobs for refusing government pressure
- Satire and social media as forms of resistance
- The blurred line between journalism and activism
- The personal cost of telling uncomfortable truths

At the heart of the story is a difficult question:
Can journalists remain neutral when democracy itself is under pressure?

This episode features interviews with Turkish journalists, editors, satirists from Leman, Kurdish reporters, and media critics from across the political spectrum.

snippet.title: Germany's Underworld: From the Harz Mountain to the North Sea
snippet.description:
Dive into Germany's hidden underwater world, where vibrant ecosystems, rare species, and centuries-old secrets await beneath tranquil lakes and rushing rivers.

In this captivating exploration of Germany's freshwater and coastal habitats, we journey from the icy rivers of the Central Highlands to the teeming mudflats of the North Sea. Discover how mighty fish like pike, carp, and the endangered sturgeon navigate life's perilous waters, and witness the seasonal transformations that shape the lives of creatures above and below the surface. From volcanic crater lakes and ancient caves to abandoned quarries revived by nature, each habitat reveals a unique web of life—where amphibians awaken in spring, newts woo their mates, and dragonflies and grass snakes thrive amid the floodplains.

Uncover the stories of elusive beavers, ancient triops, and mysterious bryozoans, alongside efforts to save the last Atlantic sturgeon and European crayfish. Spanning breathtaking scenery, forgotten histories, and cutting-edge conservation, this documentary unveils a vibrant, often overlooked aquatic universe at the heart of Germany.

In 1982, a U.S. Army sergeant stationed at one of the most sensitive American listening posts in Europe walked past the Soviet consulate in West Berlin and dropped a letter through its mail slot. By that evening he was a recruited spy.

snippet.title: Castles: The Fortresses That Ruled Medieval Europe | Extra Long Documentary
snippet.description:
For centuries, castles dominated the landscape of medieval Europe. They were symbols of power, centers of wealth, family homes and formidable military strongholds. This extra long documentary explores the fascinating world behind the castle walls, from the daily lives of nobles and servants to the engineering marvels that made these fortresses the most powerful structures of the Middle Ages. Discover how castles evolved from simple wooden fortifications around 1000 AD into vast stone complexes such as Windsor Castle, Castle Eltz, Burghausen and the legendary White Tower of London.

A second angle reveals the brutal reality of medieval warfare. From the imprisonment of Richard the Lionheart at Trifels Castle to epic sieges at Chateau Gaillard and Castle Eltz, castles became the focal points of power struggles across Europe. As trebuchets, siege towers and eventually gunpowder weapons transformed warfare between the 11th and 16th centuries, architects were forced to reinvent castle defenses. This documentary uncovers how castles shaped European history and why these iconic bastions of power continue to fascinate us today.

snippet.title: From bees to robots: The new power of swarm intelligence | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
Researchers are investigating how animals behave in swarms. Their findings are being applied to robotics, logistics and new models of participation — and are opening up new perspectives for business and democracy.


The "Imaging Hangar" at the Centre for the Advanced Study of Collective Behavior (CASAB) at the University of Konstanz is a 225-square-metre hall equipped with cameras, sensors and a 3D environment — one of the largest swarm research laboratories in the world. "Not all swarms are driven by the same motivation,” explains Iain Couzin, Director of the Institute of Behavioral Biology and spokesperson for CASAB. One of his surprising findings: "Locusts flee out of fear of being eaten by their own kind."
The "Artificial Life Lab" in Graz offers deep insights into the life of the queen bee. As part of the EU research project "RoboRoyale", biologist Thomas Schmickl observes the inner circle of a bee colony at close quarters using a robot equipped with a camera and artificial intelligence. For decades, he’s been using technology to decipher the logic of swarms. A mini-robot swarm demonstrates how young bees make faster and better decisions when working as a group.
Melanie Schranz is researching how the swarm principle could optimize a semiconductor factory in Carinthia at the "Lakeside Labs" in Klagenfurt. Products that behave like bees independently seek out the nearest available food source. In this case, that means an available machine for the next stage of production. If one machine breaks down, production continues without the need for intervention from a central command.
The logic of the many applies not only to technology, but also to society. At the "Complexity Science Hub" in Vienna, psychologist Mirta Galesic demonstrates that diversity, independence and openness are crucial to collective intelligence. She refers to this as collective adaptability.
And even democracy can be improved. "Today, it’s often a narrow majority that decides how resources are used - this leads to cronyism and discontent," warns physicist and sociologist Dirk Helbing. At ETH Zurich, he is researching new ways of participatory decision-making. "Participatory budgeting", for example, is already being trialed in many cities.
The documentary offers a fascinating glimpse behind the scenes of swarm research and highlights its potential for business and democracy.

snippet.title: Moses vs Pharaoh: The Night of Death That Changed Biblical History | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
Nine plagues had already broken Egypt. The Nile had turned red, the sky had gone dark, disease had swept the land. And still Pharaoh would not let them go. What came next was different from everything before it. Not a storm, not a swarm, not a scientific chain reaction. The death of every firstborn son in Egypt, from the palace to the slave quarters, remains the one plague that no laboratory has ever fully explained. This documentary follows scientists, archaeologists, and biblical scholars as they pursue the evidence across three thousand years of buried history. Who were the Hyksos, the mysterious foreign rulers who conquered Egypt without a battle around 1650 BC and were later expelled? Were they the historical memory behind the people of the Bible? And why does the name Israel appear for the first time not in the land of Canaan, but carved into an Egyptian stone? The answers are not where anyone expected to find them.

snippet.title: Trump and Greenland - The new rush for raw materials | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
Ever since Donald Trump started talking about acquiring Greenland, the country has become the focus of global attention. This documentary explores the island’s history and examines its strategic importance in the 21st century.

Greenland has long been more than just a barometer of climate change. But since Donald Trump’s return to the White House, the world’s largest island - autonomous, yet part of Denmark -- has become a point of contention among the major powers.

Why? As the ice sheets melt, the Arctic Ocean is opening up to shipping and resource extraction. Greenland is thus becoming a key strategic region between North America, Europe and Russia. Its vast mineral resources - ranging from oil and gas to gold and rare earths, which are indispensable for the energy transition and the defense industry - are turning the island into a new El Dorado. Mining companies and world powers alike are competing for a share.

Since Donald Trump’s re-election, the debate has become increasingly heated. In 2019, the US President publicly suggested that Greenland could be purchased by the US and accused Denmark of failing to protect the island adequately against global threats. But what lies behind these demands? How is Europe responding to American power politics? And what role can Greenland itself play in this geopolitical power struggle - caught between economic opportunities, environmental risks and the desire for sovereignty?
 
The documentary blends historical context with contemporary analysis: it shows why Greenland plays a key role in the global order today, what interests are at stake, and how the people of the island wish to shape their future.

localized.description:
Ever since Donald Trump started talking about acquiring Greenland, the country has become the focus of global attention. This documentary explores the island’s history and examines its strategic importance in the 21st century.

Greenland has long been more than just a barometer of climate change. But since Donald Trump’s return to the White House, the world’s largest island - autonomous, yet part of Denmark -- has become a point of contention among the major powers.

Why? As the ice sheets melt, the Arctic Ocean is opening up to shipping and resource extraction. Greenland is thus becoming a key strategic region between North America, Europe and Russia. Its vast mineral resources - ranging from oil and gas to gold and rare earths, which are indispensable for the energy transition and the defense industry - are turning the island into a new El Dorado. Mining companies and world powers alike are competing for a share.

Since Donald Trump’s re-election, the debate has become increasingly heated. In 2019, the US President publicly suggested that Greenland could be purchased by the US and accused Denmark of failing to protect the island adequately against global threats. But what lies behind these demands? How is Europe responding to American power politics? And what role can Greenland itself play in this geopolitical power struggle - caught between economic opportunities, environmental risks and the desire for sovereignty?
 
The documentary blends historical context with contemporary analysis: it shows why Greenland plays a key role in the global order today, what interests are at stake, and how the people of the island wish to shape their future.

snippet.title: Investigating Bukele and Trump’s Controversial CECOT Deal | FRONTLINE (PBS) + @elfaro
snippet.description:
Three months after President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025 and began his major immigration crackdown, he held a White House sit-down with a popular Latin American leader who had once called himself the world’s coolest dictator. Watch the opening scene of “The Deal: Trump, Bukele & the Gangs of El Salvador,” a new documentary from FRONTLINE and El Faro. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

As the documentary explores, Bukele opened the doors of the notorious Salvadoran prison known as CECOT to planeloads of mostly Venezuelan U.S. deportees that the Trump administration had swept up and accused of being gang members. Later reporting would reveal that most of the men had no criminal convictions in the U.S. or proven gang affiliations.

“It was pretty obvious what Trump was getting out of this deal,” T. Christian Miller of ProPublica says in the opening scene. “It was much less obvious what Bukele was doing.”

That lack of transparency was familiar to Carlos Martínez and Óscar Martínez, reporters at the El Salvador investigative news outlet El Faro who have covered Bukele and his administration for years.

“The nature of Bukele’s government is to keep things secret,” Carlos says in the opening scene. 

FRONTLINE and El Faro’s documentary, releasing April 7, pierces that veil to investigate what underpinned Bukele’s controversial CECOT deal with the Trump administration. The film chronicles how the brothers and their colleagues discovered evidence that ran counter to Bukele’s tough-on-gangs image: Bukele’s government had previously negotiated with MS-13 and other violent gangs it publicly claimed to be cracking down on, El Faro found. Those negotiations, documents showed, involved offering privileges to gang leaders in prison, in exchange for a reduction in homicides and voter support in territories the gangs controlled.

Following the revelations, Bukele, who had vowed to end government corruption and crush gangs, claimed “El Faro lied” and said the documents showing his administration’s dealings with gang leaders were “fake.” The Martínez brothers now live — and report — in exile.

Through the brothers’ story, as well as the perspectives of other reporters, former U.S. officials and insiders, “The Deal” shines new light on Bukele’s tangled history with the gangs the U.S. is fighting. The documentary examines why Bukele offered to imprison U.S. deportees in CECOT — and why, in exchange, he asked for a number of gang leaders in U.S. custody to be returned to El Salvador, in what one reporter in the documentary calls “a deal within a deal.”

Bukele has said the Trump administration's return of MS-13 members will help El Salvador "finalize intelligence gathering and go after the last remnants" of the gang. But some observers suspect he had another motive: preventing gang leaders in U.S. custody from exposing the details of their past dealings with Bukele’s administration. 

For the full story, watch “The Deal: Trump, Bukele & the Gangs of El Salvador.”

snippet.title: Hitler’s invasion of the Soviet Union: Operation Barbarossa (2/2) | DW Documentary
snippet.description:
In early September 1941, the German Wehrmacht was advancing on all fronts in the Soviet Union. Kyiv had fallen, the Smolensk stronghold had been defeated and Leningrad was under siege. Hitler intended to launch a major offensive against Moscow before the winter.

Under the code name Operation Typhoon, the ‘final battle’ began - a desperate fight for the Soviet capital. The Vyazma-Bryansk double battle was aimed at crushing Red Army units around Moscow before conquering the city itself. Initially, the Wehrmacht managed to encircle and wear down the Soviet defenders. This documentary explores the haunting remains of Yugoslavia through three abandoned sites that reveal the rise and violent collapse of a once-unified nation. Following the outbreak of the Yugoslav Wars in 1991, these locations became silent witnesses to one of Europe’s most tragic conflicts since World War II. Deep inside a mountain lies the secret Željava Air Base, a Cold War military complex destroyed during the war. Along the Adriatic coast, the once-luxurious Kupari Resort stands in ruins after being shelled in the early 1990s.

In Mostar, a city deeply scarred by the Bosnian War (1992–1995), the destruction of the iconic Stari Most bridge symbolizes the fragmentation of communities that once lived side by side. Through personal testimonies and powerful imagery, the film reveals the emotional and physical aftermath of a war that claimed approximately 150,000 lives, uncovering the fragile memory of a lost world shaped by unity, conflict, and enduring division.
